claims.head: Don’t buy Swayman’s record against the Avalanche
claims.body: Swayman has been a wall against the Avalanche since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Swayman isn’t that wall tonight.

BOS.head: The Bruins start a half-step behind
BOS.body: Even though Boston has home-ice advantage and Colorado will be without MacKinnon, the Avalanche have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Boston may be without Pastrňák. The Bruins’ best way to tip it is keeping dangerous shots away.

COL.head: The Avalanche have a slight edge

story.head: Strength vs. strength
paras: The Bruins (15-9-1) lost 3-1 to Toronto on Friday, while the Avalanche have won three straight. Going in, the Avs are second in the Central (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Bruins fifth in the Atlantic (tied for 14th).

The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (most), play the league’s fastest games (1st) and throw a lot of pucks at the net (2nd). Colorado has scored 3.96 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Bruins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd). Boston has allowed 2.72 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Bruins’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Avalanche. Beyond that, the Avalanche’s defensemen shoot a lot, and the Bruins’ not so much.

Cale Makar (5 G / 22 A / 27 P in 21 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring, and Artturi Lehkonen (17 G / 8 A / 25 P in 25 GP) has a team-high 17 goals, tied for fifth in the NHL. For the Bruins, Elias Lindholm (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Morgan Geekie (6 G / 15 A / 21 P in 25 GP) is next in line.

Mackenzie Blackwood (13-4-1 / .908 SV% in 18 GS) will likely start for Colorado, and Jeremy Swayman (11-7-1 / .899 SV% in 19 GS) for Boston. Swayman has a .934 save percentage in five starts against the Avalanche, well above his usual .903. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.

items.text: The Avalanche are newly without Martin Nečas, and have been without Nathan MacKinnon since Nov 12. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth are missing more right now.
The Bruins are newly without David Pastrňák, and have been without Michael Eyssimont and James Hagens for several games.
Brock Nelson has five goals in eight games against Boston since 2023-24, most of them with the Islanders.
With Nathan MacKinnon out, Parker Kelly took eight faceoffs in the Avalanche’s last game. He had been taking about two a game.
